change.old:
def silent(x: np.ndarray, name: str = "") -> bool:
    """non-zero in < 10% of files; or, for a continuous score only, fewer than 20 distinct values. Counts and the
    one binary indicator are exempt from the second clause: a depth of 1..12 or a yes/no is not a broken score."""
    v = x[~np.isnan(x)]
    if len(v) == 0 or (v != 0).mean() < 0.10:
        return True
    continuous = name in PREDICTORS and not PREDICTORS[name][2] and name != "risk_safety_nonzero"
    return continuous and len(np.unique(v)) < 20
change.note: the edc5c53 body (every predictor silent under 20 distinct values, no exemption for counts or the yes/no indicator) under the CURRENT signature: the edc5c53 def took no `name`, and the current callers pass one, so the literal def would only raise TypeError; the docstring is dropped as in edc5c53; trailing spaces on the last line keep the file size

D summaries of the vanished cells change too. Placebo possible: the placebo file records silence for the four primaries; it fires only if a primary count (in_degree, struct_branch, amplified_cascading_flux) has fewer than 20 distinct values in some repo clearing the HP floor - not checked, so not required. Input check possible: it compares 'silence of every predictor'; if its reference-side silence comes from the copy's own silent() it fires, if from the comparison route's rule applied to both arrays it does not (the fault-writer did not read input_check.py).
